reconcile.connective: Commentators read Ezra's "son of Levi" as a genealogical shorthand — Hebrew ben spans descendants, so Mahli is Levi's grandson through Merari.

discrepancy.connective: The objection is pressed by Steve Wells of the Skeptic's Annotated Bible, who reads Ezra 8:18's "son of Levi" against the lists that make Mahli a son of Merari and calls it a contradiction.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Mahli the son of Levi?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/mahli.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Was Mahli the son of Levi?"

excerpts.excerpt_text: He was one of the descendants of Mahli, the son, i.e., grandson, of Levi the son of Israel, i.e., Jacob: comp. Exo 6:16, Exo 6:19; Ch1 6:4.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: K&D directly glosses Ezra 8:18's 'son of Levi' as 'grandson,' tracing Mahli through Merari (Exo 6:16, 6:19) — the exact harmonization the tension turns on.

excerpts.excerpt_text: …an Israelite, of the tribe of Levi, in the line of Mahli a son of Merari, the third son of Levi …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Gill places Mahli explicitly 'in the line of Mahli a son of Merari, the third son of Levi,' resolving the apparent direct father-son claim into descent through Merari.

excerpts.excerpt_text: The Hebrew word for “sons” can also mean “descendants,” which accommodates the possibility of unnamed generations.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Tyndale states the linguistic basis for the whole harmonization — Hebrew 'son(s)' can denote 'descendants,' so 'son of Levi' need not mean a direct child.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament, on Ezra 8:18 (1861-75)
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: K&D treat this passage directly, glossing Ezra 8:18's 'son of Levi' as 'grandson' (Mahli, son of Merari, son of Levi) with cross-references to Exo 6:16, 6:19 and 1 Chr 6:4. Used in place of Haley, whose specific coverage of this exact pair could not be confirmed.
